text:
ari: quick flag: new community user hit onboarding friction with the ruby quickstart. they used REDWOOD_API_KEY but our README example uses REDWOOD_TOKEN.
jas: ack. that's been a long-standing inconsistency between sampleapps and docs. which repo/file?
ari: sampleapp README (examples/quickstart.md) shows `export REDWOOD_TOKEN=...` while the CLI and sdk both read `REDWOOD_API_KEY`. newbie ran into a 401 and thought our tokens were invalid.
mona: ugh that sucks. small but high-impact. we should standardize on REDWOOD_API_KEY across SDKs.
kyler: agreed. also add a tiny note about ephemeral tokens vs long-lived service keys so people know which to use for local dev.
jas: I'm fine with changing the sampleapp README to use REDWOOD_API_KEY. But we also need to search repo code samples and docs site for the wrong var.
ari: ran a quick grep: `git grep -n "REDWOOD_TOKEN"` shows examples in sampleapp, quickstart snippets in docs, and one test harness.
mona: propose PR steps: 1) update sampleapp README and examples, 2) update docs quickstart snippets, 3) add an automated CI smoke test that runs the quickstart with a fake key and asserts we hit the expected stubbed endpoint (prevents regressions), 4) add a small migration note in releases.
kyler: small nit: prefer env var name REDWOOD_API_KEY for parity with other SDKs, but also support a legacy fallback in SDK that reads REDWOOD_TOKEN if present, with a deprecation warning. That reduces immediate breakage for community users.
jas: i like the fallback idea. implement in sdk initializer: check ENV['REDWOOD_API_KEY'] || ENV['REDWOOD_TOKEN'] and log a one-time warn to STDERR if using legacy var. Add test that ensures fallback happens.
mona: can you also update the quickstart to show both and mark REDWOOD_TOKEN as deprecated? that helps telegraphed migration.
ari: I'll open a PR in sampleapp to update READMEs and examples. jas, can you take the SDK PR to add fallback + warning?
jas: yes. i'll add a sparse changelog entry under Unreleased and include the deprecation text and a date 3 months out for removal.
docs-bot: Reminder: docs team prefers one PR to update code snippets in the docs portal. See https://docs.redwood/authoring for guidance.
kyler: for the CI smoke test, prefer to use the local service stub we already have in CI (tests/fixtures/mock_redwood_server). Run the sampleapp quickstart against that server and assert the initial auth header is present and correct. that test should be fast and live in sampleapp CI matrix.
mona: also add a small e2e that runs the ruby quickstart script with the legacy var set to ensure the fallback message appears on STDERR.
jas: will add both tests. I'll avoid printing actual token values in logs. Use masked secrets in CI.
ari: thanks. small follow-up: could the community onboarding email/template be updated to mention the env var name change? newbies were confused.
kyler: will update the onboarding doc in growth repo.
mona: PRs?
ari: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp/pull/612 updating READMEs and adding smoke test.
jas: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-ruby/pull/611 add fallback+deprecation warning+tests.

j as: CI queued for sdk-ruby PR 611: https://ci.redwood/sdk-ruby/611 :hourglass: 
jas: updated per review comments, added test for legacy var and documented deprecation in migration notes.
docs-bot: CI passed for sdk-ruby PR 611: https://ci.redwood/sdk-ruby/611 :white_check_mark: 
mona: LGTM. merging both and will backport docs snippet to the 1.x quickstart branch as well.
ari: nice. this should reduce support tickets. :thumbsup:
